{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that line patterns with salient Gestalt information would elicit facelike holistic processing in novices without any training, evidenced by a congruency effect in an aligned composite task condition.",
  "design": "within-subjects design with factors Task (faces vs. line patterns), Alignment (aligned vs. misaligned), Congruency (congruent vs. incongruent), and Target (same vs. different top parts)",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "presentation of composite faces versus composite line patterns with salient Gestalt information (connectedness, closure, and continuity)",
  "outcome_measure": "response sensitivity (d prime) in same/different judgments of the top parts of composite stimuli",
  "population_and_setting": "22 participants tested in a laboratory setting",
  "sample_size_total": 22,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "22 people registered and participated",
  "analysis_plan": "A 2 (alignment) x 2 (congruency) x 2 (task) repeated measures ANOVA, followed by separate ANOVAs and paired t-tests for each task.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "Participants performed two composite tasks (one with faces and one with line patterns) with order counterbalanced across participants. Each trial presented a target stimulus followed by a mask and an aligned or misaligned second stimulus."
}
